title: VHF: Nhamissa Site Management — Fence Down, Team Behind the Tent

lines.text: Beira, Beira, this is Nhamissa site management, Sra. Rosa Machava. Over.

Beira, the fence at the distribution point is down on the east side. About four hundred people are inside the queue area. One older woman fell and was carried to the health post. She is conscious, and the nurse thinks it is a broken wrist. Your team of eleven is behind our tent with the stock truck. Nobody is hurt, and the truck is not damaged. But three hundred eighty-eight hygiene kits are still on it. Before the line broke, your team gave out two hundred twelve hygiene kits and four hundred twenty-four jerrycans to two hundred twelve households. Over.

Beira, more. Two of your mobilisers, Dércio and Luísa, live here at the site. They ask whether they should go home to their families or come back to Beira on the truck. The police post has two officers. They say they will not escort anything today. And your second car from Beira was due at zero nine thirty. Do I tell it to turn around? I need an answer for your people and for the car. Over.

Nhamissa, Beira. Copied all. Fence down east side, one woman injured at the health post, team of eleven safe behind your tent with the truck, three eight eight kits still loaded. Stand by for the Security Focal Point. Over.
Standing by. Please be quick, Beira. The crowd can see the truck. Nhamissa out.

fields.voiceStyle: Woman in her forties, Mozambican Portuguese accent, speaking English clearly. Controlled and practical but tense, slightly raised voice as if outdoors; Beira operator is a calm younger male.

instructorNote: Core inject: following HMSSSP 3, the SFP should stop all movements to Nhamissa at once, which turns back the 09:30 car. The SFP should also send an alert to UNDSS and the NGO safety network before the facts are confirmed, saying "an HRI distribution team" and giving no names. Under HMSSSP 6, the SFP reports to the CD within 1 hour and starts the 24-hour incident report. Watch whether the CD sets a Nhamissa threat level, decides what happens to the two resident national mobilisers (stay home with regular check-ins, or come to Beira), and approves the team's withdrawal with the truck as a movement request.

citations.documentTitle: HRI Mozambique: Staff Safety and Security Plan (decision-level summary)
citations.quote: HRI uses four threat levels: 1 (low), 2 (moderate), 3 (high, serious threat), 4 (critical). The Country Director sets the level for each area on the advice of the Security Focal Point after the SRA. F

citations.quote: Every incident (a vehicle accident, a stolen item, harassment, an arrest or detention, a threat) is reported within 1 hour to the Security Focal Point and, for a serious incident, to the Country Direc
